thread.title: Market Volatility Bulletin: Not So Sleepy Thanksgiving Week

author: The Balance of Trade
title: Market Volatility Bulletin: Not So Sleepy Thanksgiving Week
text:
Market Intro
CNBC - 11:26AM EST
Despite the green prints for much of the rest of the world, the MSCI ex-US ETF ( ACWX ) is trading about 70 basis points lower in today's session after tech ( XLK ) leads US stocks lower ( SPY , DIA , QQQ , IWM ).
CNBC.com
Spot VIX prints around its long-term average value of 19.25. The index has steadily gained ground over the course of the day.
Thoughts on Volatility
Policy changes cause alterations in patterns of trade. In any given economic cycle (or year), there are bound to be deviations from the norm based on some well-timed shift or other.
While the tariff hikes will definitely sting some industries and consumers, the real question remains whether the policy will result in net gains as it concerns IP enforcement, and better terms of trade for US companies. The jury is still out on this, and likely will remain so for a couple years.
The bump to corporate earnings only translates to higher sustainable growth if companies reinvest profits, or put better, if resources flow more efficiently through the economy. Investors, taken as a class, knew that the earnings boost from the tax reduction was a one-time boon.
My guess is that it is only a matter of time before individual tax rates (say, long-term cap gains) are raised heftily as an offset to the corporate tax cuts from last year, resulting in a more neutral proposition for investors than the one that appears today.
MacroOps shared this tweet on the current state of the EU economy. Whether a recession occurs in Europe or not remains to be seen. But what I find more interested, given the huge spread between LIBOR and Euribor, is whether it causes the Fed to hold back on rate hikes. It very likely would have in the 'data dependent' Yellen regime.
Term Structure
All the major historic and implied measures of volatility are within about three points of one another. Last week, vol shorts ( SVXY ) had their window to decisively drop SPX realized vol. Friday's closed looked promising, and the overnight session looked as though the market was going for some consolidation.
Google Finance
The week of Thanksgiving is historically one of the least volatile of the year.
Again, Friday's VIX9D reading looked as though the opportunity to dive into the mid-to-low teens was at least a possibility. Big Tech had other plans.
MarketChameleon.com - AAPL Implied Vol (Green) vs. XLK Implied Vol (Red)
Note how Apple's ( AAPL ) implied vol plunges every quarter just after the earnings announcement. This time around, however, the earnings announcement seems to have generated more questions than answers about the company's future.
Vol on the company's shares is about as high today as at any point in the year. The company makes up nearly 4% of the S&P 500. Beyond that, the shares correlate with many other equities, amplifying its capacity to cause waves for US indexes.
Conclusion If this is your first time reading Market Volatility Bulletin, thanks for giving it a try. If you're a regular, we thank you for your ongoing contributions in the comments section.
Thank you for reading.
